parts.ask: Find ∫((2/3)x³ − 1/(2x³) + 5) dx, simplifying the answer
parts.final_form: three simplified terms plus c, all on one line
parts.ms: M1 raise any power by 1; A1 two of (2/3)(x⁴/4), −(1/2)(x⁻²/−2), 5x (unsimplified); A1 two correct and simplified; A1 (1/6)x⁴ + (1/4)x⁻² + 5x + c on one line. Common slip: rewriting 1/(2x³) as 2x⁻³, which can still earn the M (MS p.8)

parts.ask: l₂ is perpendicular to l₁ and passes through (6, −2): find l₂

parts.final_form: three inequalities in x and y (not in terms of R); strict for the dashed boundary l₂ and non-strict for the solid ones, or the opposite convention used consistently
parts.ms: B1 2y ≤ x or y ≥ 2x − x²/8; M1 solve 2x − x²/8 = 0 to get x = 16 and write x < (or ≤) 16; A1 x < 16, 2y ≤ x and y ≥ 2x − x²/8 (a lower bound a ≤ x with a ≤ 12 is also allowed; strict/non-strict swapped consistently also accepted) (MS p.13)

parts.final_form: exact value of x (not ±); differentiation must be shown
parts.ms: M1 reduce a power by one; A1 f′(x) = 5x^(3/2) − 40; M1 set f′(x) = 0 and make x^(3/2) the subject, then solve; A1 x = 4 cao, not ±4 (MS p.16)

parts.ask: Solve f″(x) = 5
parts.ms: M1 differentiate f′ again and set f″(x) = 5, i.e. (15/2)x^(1/2) = 5; M1 correct method from Ax^(1/2) = 5 to x; A1 x = 4/9 or exact equivalent; no marks if no differentiation is shown (MS p.16)

parts.final_form: degrees to 1 d.p.; the obtuse angle (C lies on AD and BC = BD, so ACB is obtuse)
parts.ms: M1 sine rule sin ACB/6.5 = sin 35°/4.7 (or cosine-rule quadratic in AC, then cosine rule again); A1 awrt 52 or 53° or awrt 127 or 128°; A1 ACB = 127.5° only (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Find the total length of wood (AB, BD, BC, AD) needed
parts.final_form: nearest metre, with the unrounded total (awrt 24.1) shown
parts.ms: M1 valid method for part or all of AD (sine/cosine rule in ABD with angle ADB = 52.5°, ABD = 92.5°, or AC + CD, or right-angled triangles); A1 AD awrt 8.2; A1 total awrt 24.1, i.e. 24 m (24 or 25 alone without awrt 24.1 not accepted) (MS pp.17–20)

parts.ms: B1 y = 4 only (MS p.21)

parts.ask: State the turning point of y = f(x/4)
parts.ms: B1 (16, 9) only (MS p.21)

parts.ask: The line y = k intersects C at exactly one point: state the possible values of k
parts.final_form: values of k in terms of k (an inequality and a single value)

parts.ask: (i) y = f(x) − a passes through the origin: state a; (ii) write down another single transformation of C that passes through the origin

parts.ms: B1 (i) a = 6; B1 (ii) y = f(x − 3) (also y = f(x + 4) − 9 or y = −f(x) + 6); combinations of different transformations not accepted (MS p.21)

parts.ms: M1 multiply through by x and collect on one side; A1 2x² + (5 − c)x + 3 = 0 oe; M1 discriminant (5 − c)² − 24; dM1 set = 0 and solve for c; A1 c = 5 ± 2√6; M1 choose the inside region; A1 5 − 2√6 < c < 5 + 2√6, exact and in c (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ms: B1 one of ½r²θ = 6, 2r + rθ = 10; B1 both; M1 eliminate r (e.g. r = 10/(2 + θ)) to an equation in θ; A1* 3θ² − 13θ + 12 = 0 with (θ + 2)² expanded and an intermediate line shown (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: Hence find the possible values of r and θ
parts.final_form: exact pairs (θ, r), correctly matched; negative r rejected
parts.ms: B1 θ = 4/3, 3; M1 substitute a θ to find r; A1 θ = 4/3, r = 3 and θ = 3, r = 2, exact and correctly paired; withheld if r = −3 or −2 is not ruled out (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ms: B1 ∩-shaped quadratic; B1 through O and (3, 0); B1 negative cubic with a maximum and a minimum; B1 through O, (2, 0), (5, 0) (MS pp.26–27)

parts.ask: Show the x-coordinates of their intersections satisfy x(x² − 8x + 13) = 0
parts.ms: M1 set the curves equal; dM1 expand and collect on one side with x a factor of every term; A1* x(x² − 8x + 13) = 0 with (x − 2)(5 − x) expanded and x factored out, no errors (MS pp.26–27)

parts.ask: P lies on both curves in the first quadrant: using algebra, find the exact coordinates of P
parts.final_form: exact (surd) coordinates with working; choose the root in the first quadrant
parts.ms: M1 solve x² − 8x + 13 = 0 (formula or completing the square); A1 x = 4 ± √3; M1 substitute 4 − √3 into a curve; M1 surd working shown to reach d + f√g; A1 (4 − √3, −7 + 5√3) as the only answer. Roots stated without working: at most M0A0M1M1A0 (MS pp.26–27)

parts.final_form: y = mx + c with integers m, c
parts.ms: M1 substitute x = 4 into dy/dx as given (not differentiated); A1 gradient 19; M1 line through (4, −2) with their gradient (via y = mx + c: must reach c); A1 y = 19x − 78 cao (MS p.28)

parts.ask: Find f(x)
parts.ms: M1 raise a power by 1; A1 one term correct; A1 both, (6/5)x^(5/2) − 20x^(1/2); M1 substitute (4, −2) to find c; A1 f(x) = (6/5)x^(5/2) − 20x^(1/2) − 0.4 cso (MS p.28)

parts.ms: M1 reduce a correct power by one on either x term; A1 one of (3/8)x², 12x^(−3/2) correct and simplified; A1 dy/dx = (3/8)x² + 12x^(−3/2) or exact simplified equivalent (MS p.8)

parts.ask: P(4, −3) lies on C: find the tangent to C at P
parts.final_form: y = mx + c with m and c found
parts.ms: M1 evaluate their dy/dx at x = 4 (7.5); M1 tangent through (4, −3) with that gradient (via y = mx + c: must reach c); A1 y = 7.5x − 33 or exact equivalent; a calculator gradient without the derivative can earn the last two marks (MS p.8)

parts.final_form: a + b√2 with rational a, b
parts.ms: M1 multiply numerator and denominator by (4 + 2√2); A1 1/2 + (1/4)√2 or exact equivalent (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Hence or otherwise solve 4x = 2√2x + 20√2, giving x in the form p + q√2 with p, q rational
parts.final_form: p + q√2 with rational p, q
parts.ms: M1 collect x terms, x(4 − 2√2) = 20√2; dM1 use (a): x = 20√2 × (1/2 + √2/4); A1 10 + 10√2, not 10(√2 + 1), and only with the step using (a) seen; squaring to a quadratic or rationalising afresh are alternative routes (MS pp.9–10)

parts.final_form: given inequality from a linear inequality in x
parts.ms: M1 perimeter, 2 × 5x + 2(6x − 2); dM1 set > 29 and solve to ax > c; A1* x > 1.5 with an intermediate line such as 22x > 33, cso (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Given also that the area is less than 72 m², form and solve a quadratic inequality in x

parts.ms: M1 area as a sum or difference of rectangles, e.g. 2x(2x − 1) + 3x(6x − 2); A1 22x² − 8x − 72 < 0 oe simplified; M1 critical values of the 3TQ (x = −18/11, 2); ddM1 inside region; A1 −18/11 < x < 2 (0 < x < 2 also allowed in context) (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Hence state the range of possible values of x
parts.ms: B1 1.5 < x < 2; "x > 1.5 or x < 2" not accepted (MS p.11)

parts.final_form: simplest form, plus constant of integration
parts.ms: M1 split into Px^m + Qx^n with an index processed; A1 2x^(3/2) + (1/2)x^(−1/2); M1 raise a correct index by 1; A1 one term correct and simplified; A1 (4/5)x^(5/2) + x^(1/2) + c (MS p.11)

parts.ms: M1 take out the factor x; dM1 solve the quadratic algebraically; A1 x = −5, 0, 7/2. Calculator answers only, or the quadratic formula applied to the cubic, score 0 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Hence find all real solutions of 2(y − 5)⁶ + 3(y − 5)⁴ − 35(y − 5)² = 0
parts.final_form: all real solutions, exact; reject the negative value of (y − 5)²

parts.ask: y = f(x + a) passes through the origin: state the possible values of a
parts.ms: B1 one of −1/2, 4; B1 a = −1/2 and 4 only (MS p.20)

parts.ask: Smallest positive solution of sin(x/12) = k is α: find in terms of α (i) the negative solution of sin(x/12) = k closest to zero, (ii) the smallest positive solution of cos(x/12) = k

parts.ask: Expand f(x) to ax³ + bx² + cx + d

parts.ask: Find the gradient of the tangent to y = x² + 3x − 2 at P(3, 16)
parts.ms: M1 dy/dx = 2x + 3 at x = 3; A1 9 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Q on the curve has x-coordinate 3 + h: find the gradient of chord PQ in terms of h
parts.ms: B1 y_Q = (3 + h)² + 3(3 + h) − 2; M1 (y_Q − 16)/h; A1 9 + h with no errors, not from calculus (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Explain the relationship between the chord gradient in (b) and the tangent gradient in (a)
parts.final_form: statement about the limit as h → 0
parts.ms: B1 as h → 0 the chord gradient tends to 9, the tangent gradient; needs 9 + h and 9 and a reference to the limit (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Rectangle ABCD with AB = 16 m; sector APCOA centre O on DC, radius 12 m: show angle AOD = 1.231 rad to 3 d.p.
parts.final_form: given value to 3 d.p. with working
parts.ms: M1 cos AOD = 4/12 (OD = 16 − 12) or another valid route (Pythagoras then sine/tangent, cosine rule); A1* awrt 1.231 with a step shown (in degrees, awrt 70.5° must appear first) (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Find the area of the lawn APCDA
parts.ms: M1 ½r²θ with r = 12 and θ = π ± 1.231 or 1.231; M1 area of triangle AOD, ½ × 4 × √(12² − 4²) (≈ 22.6); ddM1 major sector − triangle, ½ × 12² × (π + 1.231) − 22.6, or circle − minor sector − triangle; A1 awrt 292.2 m² (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Find the perimeter of the lawn
parts.ms: M1 arc rθ with r = 12 and an allowable angle; dM1 P = 16 + √(12² − 4²) + 12(π + 1.231); A1 awrt 79.8 m (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Find, using algebra, all solutions of 20x³ − 50x² − 30x = 0
parts.ms: M1 factorise out x (e.g. 10x(2x² − 5x − 3)); A1 two of 0, −1/2, 3; A1 all three, nothing else; answers only score 0 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Hence find all real solutions of 20(y + 3)^(3/2) − 50(y + 3) − 30(y + 3)^(1/2) = 0
parts.final_form: all real solutions; reject values impossible for (y + 3)^(1/2)
parts.ms: B1ft set (y + 3)^(1/2) equal to a root from (a); M1 square and subtract 3 for a non-zero root; A1ft y = 6; A1 y = −3 and 6, with −1/2 rejected (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: l₁: 3x − 4y + 20 = 0; l₂ through R(8, 0) parallel to l₁: find l₂
parts.final_form: ax + by + c = 0 with integers a, b, c
parts.ms: M1 gradient of l₁ (3/4); M1 line through R(8, 0) with the same gradient (via y = mx + c: must reach c); A1 3x − 4y − 24 = 0 or an integer multiple, seen in (a) (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: l₁ meets the axes at P and Q; PQRS is a parallelogram: find its area
parts.ms: B1 P(−20/3, 0) and Q(0, 5); M1 area = PR × OQ = (8 + 20/3) × 5 (shoelace or determinant also accepted); A1 220/3 (awrt 73.3 condoned) (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Find the coordinates of S
parts.ms: M1 full method for both coordinates of S (OP + QR as vectors, intersecting lines, or equal-length equations); A1 S(4/3, −5). S = (44/3, 5), from the parallelogram PQSR, scores SC 1,0 (MS pp.14–16)

parts.ask: From a sketch of y = 3 sin x (degrees), state the coordinates of the marked points P and Q
parts.ms: M1 one value of (90°, 3); A1 P(90°, 3); B1 Q(540°, 0); radians or missing brackets penalised once (MS p.18)

parts.ask: C₂: y = 3 sin x + k has maximum value 10; state the minimum point R with the smallest positive x-coordinate
parts.ms: M1 one value of (270°, 4); A1 R(270°, 4) (k = 7, so the minimum value is 4) (MS p.18)

parts.ask: Find the set of k for which y = k(2x − 1) does not cross or touch y = x² + 2x + 11
parts.ms: M1 equate k(2x − 1) = x² + 2x + 11; A1 x² + (2 − 2k)x + 11 + k = 0; M1 discriminant to a 3TQ in k (4k² − 12k − 40) and critical values; A1 k = 5, −2 from correct working; M1 inside region (b² − 4ac < 0); A1 −2 < k < 5 cso (in x: A0) (MS p.19)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: y = (4x² + 9)/(2√x), x > 0; find the x-coordinate where dy/dx = 0
parts.ms: M1 divide by 2√x into powers (one term correct); A1 2x^(3/2) + (9/2)x^(−1/2); M1 differentiate a power; A1 3x^(1/2) − (9/4)x^(−3/2); M1 set = 0 and manipulate to x² = … (or x⁴ = …); A1 x = √3/2 cso, negative root rejected. Rounded 0.87 with no working: M0A0. Quotient or product rule also accepted (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: Sketch y = (4x − 3)(x − 5)², showing axis intercepts
parts.final_form: labelled sketch with touching point at the repeated root
parts.ms: B1 positive cubic shape; B1 crosses at (3/4, 0) and touches at (5, 0); B1 y-intercept (0, −75) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: (i) find x for which f(x/4) = 0; (ii) find p so that y = f(x) + p passes through the origin
parts.final_form: values of x; value of p
parts.ms: B1ft (i) x = 3, 20 (4 × their roots), nothing else; B1ft (ii) p = 75 (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: g(x) = f(x + 1): (i) find g(x) in simplest (factorised allowed) form; (ii) hence find the y-intercept of C₂
parts.ms: M1 replace x with x + 1; A1 g(x) = (4x + 1)(x − 4)² or 4x³ − 31x² + 56x + 16; B1 16 or (0, 16) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: f″(x) = 6/√(x³) + x, P(4, −50) on the curve, f′(4) = −4: find the normal at P
parts.ms: B1 normal gradient 1/4; M1 line through (4, −50) with the changed gradient; A1 y = x/4 − 51 (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: Find f(x) (integrate twice, using f′(4) = −4 then P)
parts.ms: M1 integrate f″ with one index correct; A1 −12x^(−1/2) + x²/2 (+k); dM1 use f′(4) = −4; A1 k = −6; dM1 integrate again; A1ft −24x^(1/2) + x³/6 − 6x (+d); dddM1 use (4, −50) for d (both constants present); A1 f(x) = −24x^(1/2) + x³/6 − 6x + 34/3, exact (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: Given (3pq²)⁴ × 2p√(q⁸) ≡ a p^b q^c, find a, b and c
parts.ms: B1 a = 162; B1 b = 5; B1 c = 12; values may be implied by the expression (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Express f(x) = 3 + 12x − 2x² in the form a − b(x + c)²
y = f(x) − 7 crosses the x-axis at P and Q and the y-axis at R: find the area of triangle PQR
parts.ms: B1 R(0, −4); M1 solve f(x) − 7 = 0 (x = 3 ± √7); dM1 area = ½ × (difference of roots) × 4; A1 4√7 (√112 or 2√28 also accepted) cao. Using f(x) + 7 instead scores B0M1M1A0 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Badge: two congruent triangles AOC, BOC (AO = OB = 3 cm, OC = 5 cm) joined to sector AOB of angle α; sector area 7.2 cm²: show α = 1.6 rad
parts.final_form: given value with ½r²θ working shown
parts.ms: M1 ½ × 3² × α = 7.2 solved for α (or α = 1.6 substituted to give 7.2); A1* α = 1.6 with an intermediate line and a conclusion (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Hence find (i) the area of the badge, (ii) the perimeter of the badge
parts.final_form: (i) cm² to 2 significant figures; (ii) cm to 1 decimal place
parts.ms: (i) M1 angle COA = (2π − 1.6)/2 ≈ 2.34; M1 triangle area ½ × 5 × 3 sin(2.34) (≈ 5.38); dM1 2 × triangle + 7.2; A1 awrt 18 cm². (ii) B1 arc AB = 4.8; M1 AC by the cosine rule (AC² ≈ 54.9); dM1 2AC + 4.8; A1 awrt 19.6 cm (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Solve simultaneously y − 3x = 4 and x² + y² + 6x − 4y = 4, showing all stages of working
parts.final_form: all (x, y) solution pairs from algebraic substitution
parts.ms: M1 substitute y = 3x + 4 (or x = (y − 4)/3) into the circle equation; M1 collect to a 3TQ; A1 5x² + 9x − 2 = 0 (or 5y² − 13y − 46 = 0); dM1 solve with working (calculator roots: dM0 and final A0); B1 x = 0.2, −2 (or y = 4.6, −2); M1 find the other coordinate; A1 (0.2, 4.6) and (−2, −2), correctly paired (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Curve y = f(x) through (−5, 0), (0, −3), touching the x-axis at (2, 0): on separate diagrams sketch (a) y = f(x + 2), (b) y = f(−x)
parts.final_form: two sketches showing coordinates of all axis crossings/touching points
parts.ms: (a) B1 negative cubic translated left; B1 maximum (touching point) at the origin; B1 crosses at (−7, 0). (b) B1 reflection in the y-axis (positive cubic, minimum in quadrant 4, not on the y-axis); B1 touches at (−2, 0) and crosses at (5, 0); B1 through (0, −3). Coordinates without a sketch score nothing (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: y = k cos(x + π/6), 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, meets the y-axis at (0, √3) and the x-axis at (p, 0), (q, 0): find k and exact p, q
parts.final_form: k; exact values of p and q in terms of π
parts.ms: B1 k = 2 (k cos(π/6) = √3); B1 p = π/3 or q = 4π/3 (awrt 1.05 or 4.19, or 60° or 240°, accepted); B1 both exact (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: A(−4, 11), B(8, 2): find the gradient of AB
parts.ms: M1 gradient method; A1 −3/4 (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: l passes through the midpoint M of AB, perpendicular to AB: find l
parts.final_form: px + qy + r = 0 with integers p, q, r
parts.ms: B1 M(2, 13/2); M1 perpendicular gradient 4/3; M1 line through M with the changed gradient (via y = mx + c: must reach c); A1 8x − 6y + 23 = 0 or an integer multiple (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: C lies on l with area of triangle ABC = 37.5: find both possible coordinates of C
parts.ms: M1 AB = 15 by Pythagoras; M1 ½ × MC × AB = 37.5, so MC = 5; dM1 strategy for C on l (steps of ±3 in x and ±4 in y, or a circle of radius 5 about M with l); A1 one of (−1, 2.5), (5, 10.5); A1 both, correctly paired (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Sketch y = 1/(2 − x)
parts.final_form: sketch with axis intersection coordinates and asymptote equations stated
parts.ms: B1 reciprocal shape with branches top left and bottom right of the asymptotes; B1 intercept (0, 1/2) only; B1 asymptotes x = 2 and y = 0 only ("x-axis" not accepted); no marks without a sketch (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: y = 4x + k meets C at two distinct points: show that k² + 16k + 48 > 0
parts.final_form: given inequality via the discriminant of the resulting quadratic
parts.ms: M1 equate, multiply by (2 − x) and collect; A1 4x² + (k − 8)x + 1 − 2k = 0 oe; M1 discriminant (k − 8)² − 16(1 − 2k); A1* k² + 16k + 48 > 0 with b² − 4ac > 0 stated, no errors (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Hence find the range of possible values of k
parts.final_form: solution set of the quadratic inequality (two separate intervals)
parts.ms: M1 solve the quadratic (calculator roots acceptable); A1 k = −12, −4; M1 outside region; A1 k < −12 or k > −4 in terms of k ("and", −12 > k > −4 or −4 < k < −12 not accepted) (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: y = (x − 2)(x − 4)²: show that dy/dx = 3x² − 20x + 32
parts.ms: M1 expand to x³ ± …x² ± …x ± 32; A1 x³ − 10x² + 32x − 32; M1 differentiate a term; A1* dy/dx = 3x² − 20x + 32 with no errors (product rule alternative) (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Find the tangent l₁ to C at x = 6
parts.final_form: y = mx + c with m and c found
parts.ms: B1 y = 16 at x = 6; B1 gradient 20; M1 tangent through (6, 16) with that gradient (via y = mx + c: must reach c); A1 y = 20x − 104 cao (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Tangent l₂ at x = α is parallel to and distinct from l₁: find α
parts.ms: M1 set 3x² − 20x + 32 equal to their 20, giving a 3TQ; dM1 solve it; A1 α = 2/3. Solving 3x² − 20x + 32 = 0 (giving 4 and 8/3) scores 0 (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: f′(x) = 27x² − (21x³ − 5x)/(2√x), x > 0, curve through (9, 10): find f(x)
parts.final_form: each term fully simplified, constant evaluated
parts.ms: M1 split the fraction with one correct index ((21/2)x^(5/2) or (5/2)x^(1/2)); M1 raise a power by 1; A1 two terms; A1 all of 9x³ − 3x^(7/2) + (5/3)x^(3/2); dM1 use f(9) = 10 to find c; A1 f(x) = 9x³ − 3x^(7/2) + (5/3)x^(3/2) − 35, simplified (MS p.23)

parts.ask: Differentiate y = 2x³ − 5x² − 3/(2x) + 7 (x > 0)
parts.ms: M1 any power reduced by 1; A1 two of 6x², −10x, +(3/2)x⁻² simplified; A1 all three on one line, e.g. 6x² − 10x + 3/(2x²) (not −10x¹ or + −10x) (MS p.7)

parts.ask: P on the curve has x-coordinate 1/2: find the normal at P
parts.final_form: ax + by + c = 0 with integers a, b, c
parts.ms: B1 y = 3 at x = 1/2; M1 substitute x = 1/2 into their dy/dx (5/2); dM1 normal gradient −2/5 by the perpendicular rule; M1 line through (1/2, 3) with the changed gradient (if y = mx + c used, must reach c); A1 2x + 5y − 16 = 0 or integer multiple, must include = 0 (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: Tree height model H³ = pt² + q with H = 2 at t = 3 and H = 2.4 at t = 5: find p and q
parts.ms: M1 use the model at least once, e.g. 2³ = 9p + q; A1 9p + q = 8 and 25p + q = 13.824; dM1 solve simultaneously for p or q; A1 p = 0.364, q = 4.724 (fractions 91/250, 1181/250 accepted); correct values with no working score 4 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find T when the height is 5 m according to the model
parts.ms: M1 make T² = (125 − q)/p with H = 5 and proceed to T (needs (125 − q)/p > 0); A1 T = 18.2 cao (MS p.9)

parts.ask: From a sketch of y = 4 cos x°, state the coordinates of the marked points P and Q
parts.ms: B1 one coordinate of P, B1 P(−180, −4) in degrees; B1 Q(450, 0); reversed coordinates score B1B0 (SC); radians throughout capped at one mark per point (MS p.10)

parts.ask: C₂: y = 4 cos x° + k has minimum value −1; state the maximum point R with the smallest positive x-coordinate
parts.ms: B1 x = 360 or y = 7; B1 R(360, 7) in degrees; (7, 360) scores B1B0 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Line l through P(−2, 13) and Q(4, −5): find its equation
parts.final_form: y = mx + c with integers m, c
parts.ms: B1 gradient −3; M1 line through P or Q with their gradient (perpendicular gradient M0; y = mx + c must reach c); A1 y = −3x + 7 cso (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Quadratic C passes through P and has its minimum at Q: find an equation for C
parts.ms: M1 use minimum (4, −5), e.g. y = A(x − 4)² − 5, or with ax² + bx + c via dy/dx = 0 at x = 4 or symmetry; dM1 substitute (−2, 13) to find A (or solve the three equations); A1 y = ½(x − 4)² − 5 or y = ½x² − 4x + 3 (not 'C = …') (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Define with inequalities the region R in the second quadrant bounded by C and l only
parts.ms: M1 two of y > −3x + 7, y < ½(x − 4)² − 5, x < −2 (line must have negative gradient, curve positive quadratic); A1 all three and no others (x < k for k between −2 and 4 accepted; consistent ≥/≤ allowed; set notation needs ∩ not ∪) (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Viewing platform: sector ABCOA (OA = OC = 6 m) joined to triangle AOD with AD = 14 m, angle ADC = 0.43 rad, angle AOD obtuse, OCD straight: find angle AOD
parts.final_form: radians to 3 decimal places; obtuse (ambiguous case of the sine rule)
parts.ms: M1 sine rule sin α/14 = sin 0.43/6 (or awrt 1.33/1.34 rad, 76.6/76.7° seen); A1 acute angle awrt 1.33/1.34; A1 angle AOD = π − 1.337 = awrt 1.805 rad (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the length of arc ABC
parts.ms: M1 s = rθ with r = 6 and an allowable angle (their (a), π − (a) or 2π − (a)); A1 awrt 26.9 m from the reflex angle 2π − 1.805; using acute AOD gives 29.7, M1A0 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the total area of the platform (sector plus triangle)
parts.ms: M1 sector ½r²θ with r = 6 and an allowable angle (80.6); M1 triangle AOD = ½ × 6 × 14 × sin(π − 0.43 − (a)) (≈ 33.1) or equivalent correct method; dM1 add both correct areas; A1 awrt 113.7 m²; acute-angle route gives 130, M1M1dM1A0 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Sketch y = −k/x, k > 0
parts.ms: M1 negative-reciprocal shape (top-left and bottom-right branches) with no clear overlaps; A1 correct curve in quadrants 2 and 4 only, asymptotic to the axes (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: On a separate diagram sketch y = −k/x + k
parts.final_form: sketch with x-intercept coordinates and horizontal asymptote equation in terms of k
parts.ms: B1ft graph of (a) translated up; B1 x-intercept (1, 0) or asymptote y = k; B1 both stated (just k on the asymptote line not enough); graph takes precedence over contradictory text (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: Find the range of k for which y = −k/x + k does not touch or intersect y = 3x + 4
parts.ms: M1 set 3x + 4 = −k/x + k and reach a 3TQ; A1 3x² + (4 − k)x + k = 0; M1 b² − 4ac = k² − 20k + 16 used to find critical values (needs a = 3, b and c in k); dM1 b² − 4ac < 0 and inside region chosen; A1 10 − 2√21 < k < 10 + 2√21 (or exact equivalent; 'or' between the two inequalities not accepted) (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: f(x) = 2x − 3√x − 5 (x > 0); solve f(x) = 9 (quadratic in √x)
parts.final_form: exact solution(s); reject the impossible value of √x
parts.ms: No calculator: answers without working score 0. M1 2x − 3√x − 14 = 0 solved as a 3TQ in √x (factorised form, formula or completed square shown), or isolate and square to a 3TQ; A1 √x = 7/2 (or 4x² − 65x + 196 = 0); dM1 find a value of x; A1 x = 49/4 only, 4 rejected if found (MS pp.17–19)

parts.ask: Solve f″(x) = 6
parts.ms: B1 f′(x) = 2 − (3/2)x^(−1/2); M1 differentiate again (an index reduced by 1); A1 f″(x) = (3/4)x^(−3/2); dM1 set = 6 and make x the subject with an intermediate step (e.g. x^(−3/2) = 8); A1 x = 1/4 cso, working shown (MS pp.17–19)

parts.ask: For f(x) = (3x − 2)²(x − 4) (sketch given), deduce the values of x for which f(x) > 0
parts.ms: B1 x > 4 only (MS p.19)

parts.ask: Expand f(x) to ax³ + bx² + cx + d
parts.ms: M1 multiply two brackets then the third (x terms from a genuine product); A1 two terms of 9x³ − 48x² + 52x − 16 correct and simplified; A1 all four (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Line l through the y-intercept of C, parallel to the x-axis, cuts C again at P and Q; using algebra (no calculator-only solutions), find PQ
parts.ms: B1ft 9x³ − 48x² + 52x = 0 from setting their cubic = −16; M1 cancel x to a 3TQ and solve (calculator fine once the 3TQ is shown; not available if their quadratic factorises); B1 roots (16 ± 4√3)/6 (awrt 1.51, 3.82); M1 subtract the two non-zero roots; A1 (4/3)√3 exact cso, all previous marks needed; solving f(x) = 0 scores 0 (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: Integrate (3x + 2)²/(4√x) with respect to x, x > 0
parts.final_form: simplest form, plus constant of integration
parts.ms: M1 expand and divide by 4√x, one correct index (e.g. (9/4)x^(3/2)); dM1 raise a correct index by 1; A1 one of (9/10)x^(5/2), 2x^(3/2), 2x^(1/2); A1 two correct; A1 all three + c on one line (0.9 accepted; ignore ∫ or dx left in) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: f′(x) = x² + ax + b; y-intercept −8; P(3, −2) on C; gradient 2 at P: find f(x)
parts.final_form: f(x) in simplest form with all constants found
parts.ms: M1 f′(3) = 2 gives 9 + 3a + b = 2; M1 integrate to …x³ + …ax² + bx (+c); dM1 use c = −8 and (3, −2); A1 −2 = 9 + (9/2)a + 3b − 8; ddM1 solve for a and b (a = −4, b = 5); A1 f(x) = x³/3 − 2x² + 5x − 8 as final answer, no isw (multiplying through by 3 loses it) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Differentiate y = x²/3 + 4/√x + 8/(3x) − 5 (x > 0)
parts.ms: M1 any power reduced by 1; A1 one, A1 two of (2/3)x, −2x^(−3/2), −(8/3)x⁻² (exact simplified equivalents); A1 all three simplified on one line, no isw and no rounded decimals (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the equation of the normal to C at P(4, 3)
parts.final_form: ax + by + c = 0 with integers a, b, c
parts.ms: M1 substitute x = 4 into their dy/dx (9/4); M1 normal gradient by −1/m (−4/9); dM1 line through (4, 3) with the changed gradient (y = mx + c must reach c); A1 4x + 9y − 43 = 0 or integer multiple with all terms on one side (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: f(x) = ax³ + (6a + 8)x² − a²x, a > 0, f(−1) = 32; (i) show a = 3 is the only possible value; (ii) with a = 3 solve f(x) = 0
parts.final_form: (i) reject the other root of the quadratic in a using a > 0; (ii) all roots exactly
parts.ms: (i) M1 substitute x = −1, f = 32 and reach a 3TQ in a; dM1 solve with working shown ((a + 8)(a − 3), formula or completed square; roots just stated get dM0); A1* a = 3 or −8, choose a = 3 with a reason such as a > 0 (crossing out −8 alone is A0). (ii) M1 take out x and solve the quadratic with an intermediate step; A1 x = 0, 1/3, −9; no working scores 0 (MS pp.8–10)

parts.ask: Hence find all real solutions of (i) 3y + 26y^(2/3) − 9y^(1/3) = 0 and (ii) 3(9^(3z)) + 26(9^(2z)) − 9(9^z) = 0
parts.final_form: all real solutions; reject values impossible for the substituted quantity
parts.ms: (i) B1 y = 0; M1 set y^(1/3) equal to a non-zero root from (a) and cube, working seen; A1 y = 1/27, −729 and no others besides 0. (ii) M1 set 9^z equal to a positive root (9^z = 1/3) and solve (logs allowed); A1 z = −1/2 only; answers without working or calculator-only score 0 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: triangle ABC with AB = p, AC = q, BC = 2√2, angle BAC = 60°; show that p² + q² − pq = 8
parts.final_form: given equation via the cosine rule with cos 60° used exactly
parts.ms: M1 cosine rule (2√2)² = p² + q² − 2pq cos 60° (or two right-angled triangles taken to an equation); A1* p² + q² − pq = 8 with no errors, a line of working required (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Given AC is 2 m longer than AB, use algebra to find the exact values of p and q
parts.final_form: exact (surd) values; reject the negative root
parts.ms: M1 substitute q = p + 2; A1 p² + 2p − 4 = 0 (or q² − 2q − 4 = 0); M1 solve by formula (values embedded) or completing the square, factorising or stated roots M0; B1 p = −1 + √5 or q = 1 + √5 exact; A1 cso both and only these values (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Using (b), calculate the exact area of the flower bed
parts.ms: M1 ½ × (−1 + √5)(1 + √5) × sin 60° with working; A1 √3 m² exact, rounded answers not accepted (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Integrate (3√x + 2)(x − 5)/(4√x) with respect to x (expand and divide first)
parts.final_form: each term in simplest form, plus constant of integration
parts.ms: M1 split into a sum of powers, one correct index from correct work; A1 two, A1 all four of (3/4)x − 15/4 + ½x^(1/2) − (5/2)x^(−1/2); dM1 raise a power by 1; A1 two integrated terms correct (indices processed); A1 (3/8)x² − (15/4)x + (1/3)x^(3/2) − 5x^(1/2) + C simplified on one line (−(15/4)x¹ not accepted) (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Share models P_A = 53 − 0.4(t − 8)², P_B = −1.6t + 44.2 (t ≥ 0, £ millions): find the difference in value at t = 0
parts.ms: M1 substitute t = 0 into P_A and subtract from 44.2; A1 awrt £16.8 million (MS p.14)

parts.ask: State the maximum share value of company A during the 15 years
parts.ms: B1 £53 million (condone 53) (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Using algebra with working, find the times in the 15-year period when A's value exceeds B's
parts.final_form: interval of t from solving a quadratic inequality, restricted to the period
parts.ms: M1 set −1.6t + 44.2 = 53 − 0.4(t − 8)² (any inequality sign allowed); M1 rearrange to a 3TQ (0.4t² − 8t + 16.8 = 0) and solve, calculator roots acceptable; A1 t = 10 − √58 = awrt 2.38; A1ft 2.38 < t up to the upper limit 15 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Explain why the model for A should not be used to predict its value at t = 20
parts.ms: B1 the share value would become negative, or the model is only known to hold for 15 years; a bare '−4.6 < 0' without reference to the model is insufficient (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: x > 0, f′(x) = 32/(3x²) + 3 − 2∛x, P(8, 2) on C: find the tangent at P
parts.final_form: y = mx + c with m and c found
parts.ms: M1 f′(8) = −5/6; dM1 line through (8, 2) with their f′(8) (y = mx + c must reach c); A1 y = −(5/6)x + 26/3 (MS p.16)

parts.ask: Find f(x) in simplest form
parts.ms: M1 raise one power (x⁻² → x⁻¹, 3 → 3x, x^(1/3) → x^(4/3)); A1 two of −(32/3)x⁻¹, +3x, −(3/2)x^(4/3); A1 all three (+c condoned); dM1 substitute (8, 2) to find c; A1 f(x) = −(32/3)x⁻¹ + 3x − (3/2)x^(4/3) + 10/3, no rounded decimal coefficients, isw (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: l₁: 4y + 3x = 48 cuts the y-axis at C: state the y-coordinate of C
parts.ms: B1 12; the main working takes precedence over the diagram if they conflict (MS p.18)

parts.ask: l₂ passes through D(8, 6) on l₁ and is perpendicular to l₁: show l₂ meets the y-axis at E with y = −14/3
parts.ms: B1 gradient of l₁ = −3/4 identified or used; M1 perpendicular gradient 4/3 and line through (8, 6) (y = mx + c must reach c); A1* y = −14/3 cso, clearly stated as the y-coordinate (MS pp.18–19)

parts.ask: Sector BCE with centre C has angle 1.8 rad: find the arc length BE
parts.ms: B1ft radius CE = 12 + 14/3 = 50/3; M1 arc = r × 1.8; A1 30 cao (MS pp.18–19)

parts.ask: Calculate the exact area of region CBED (sector BCE plus triangle CDE)
parts.ms: M1 sector ½ × (50/3)² × 1.8 (= 250); M1 add triangle CDE by a correct method (CD = 10, DE = 40/3, area 200/3; shoelace also fine); A1 950/3 cao (316⅔ or 316.6 accepted, not 316.7) (MS pp.18–19)

parts.ask: Write 3x² + 6x + 9 in the form a(x + b)² + c
parts.final_form: a(x + b)² + c with constants found
parts.ms: B1 3(x ± …)² ± … or a = 3; M1 3(x + 1)² ± … (a = 3 and b = 1); A1 3(x + 1)² + 6 (equating coefficients also fine) (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: Deduce the minimum point P of C₁
parts.ms: B1ft (−1, 6) or their (−b, c) (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: Cubic C₂: y = Ax³ + Bx² + Cx + D passes through P and meets the x-axis at −4, −2 and 3: find A, B, C, D, making the method clear
parts.ms: B1 factors (x + 4)(x + 2)(x − 3); M1 substitute P(−1, 6) to find the scale factor; A1 −1/2; M1 expand to x³ + … − 24 (times scale factor); A1 A = −1/2, B = −3/2, C = 5, D = 12. Alt: B1 three equations from the roots, M1 fourth from P, A1 one value, M1 solve (calculator/matrices fine), A1 all four (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: For y = tan x on −2π ≤ x ≤ 2π, state an equation of the marked asymptote l
parts.ms: B1 x = 3π/2 oe, an equation, not degrees; if several given it must be identified (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: (i) On the diagram sketch y = 1/x + 1, stating its horizontal asymptote; (ii) hence, giving a reason, state the number of solutions of tan x = 1/x + 1 in −2π ≤ x ≤ 2π
parts.final_form: sketch with asymptote equation; a number with a reason referring to intersections of the curves
parts.ms: (i) B1 1/x-type branch in quadrant 1 not crossing the axes; B1 both branches correctly placed with asymptote labelled y = 1. (ii) B1 5 only; B1 reason: solutions = points of intersection of the two graphs (not where they cross the x-axis) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: State the number of solutions of tan x = 1/x + 1 in (i) 0 ≤ x ≤ 40π, (ii) −10π ≤ x ≤ 5π/2
parts.ms: (i) B1ft 40 (follow through their sketch, e.g. first-quadrant intersections × 20); (ii) B1 14 (MS pp.22–23)

parts.final_form: each term in simplest form, plus constant of integration
parts.ms: M1 xⁿ → xⁿ⁺¹ on at least one term, index processed; A1A1A1A1 one, two, three, then all of 3x⁴, (1/3)x^(1/2), (1/2)x⁻³ and +c (+c counts as a term), the last needing everything simplified on one line; spurious ∫ or '= 0' with no clean expression loses the final mark (MS p.7)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: y = 3x⁵ + 4x³ − x + 5 has gradient 2 at P and Q; find their x-coordinates (quadratic in x²)
parts.final_form: exact x-coordinates of both points; reject impossible values of x²
parts.ms: M1 differentiate, one correct power; A1 15x⁴ + 12x² − 1; dM1 set = 2 and form a 3TQ in x² (15x⁴ + 12x² − 3 = 0); ddM1 solve it for x² with working (stated roots from the correct quadratic score M0); A1 x = ±1/√5 (both needed; exact equivalents such as ±√5/5), isw (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Solve the inequality 3/x > 4
parts.ms: B1 critical values 0 and 3/4 (from 3x < 4x² or a sketch); M1 choose the inside region; A1 0 < x < 3/4 (equivalents such as x > 0 and x < 3/4); a common special case, x < 3/4 only, scores B1 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Infinite region R in quadrants 2 and 3 bounded only by C: y = 2x² − 50 and line l (gradient 3, meeting C on the negative x-axis): define R with inequalities
parts.final_form: inequalities in x and y (equation of l found first)
parts.ms: B1 l: y = 3(x + 5) (y = 3x + 15); M1 two of y < 2x² − 50, y > 3x + 15, x < a with −5 ≤ a ≤ 6.5 (inequalities written in terms of R score M0); A1 all three; consistent strictness needed if a = −5, set notation needs ∩ (MS pp.9–10)

parts.final_form: coordinates of Q; value of k
parts.ms: (i) B1 one coordinate, B1 Q(90, −1) ((−1, 90) scores SC B1B0); (ii) B1 k = 225; radians penalised once only (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Given cos 2x° = p has exactly two solutions in 0 ≤ x ≤ k, find the range of p
parts.final_form: range of p, plus any isolated value of p that also gives exactly two solutions; check end-point inclusion
parts.ms: M1 one of −1 < p < 0 or p = 1 (ft their minimum value from (a); condone y for p here); A1 both, in terms of p (MS p.11)

parts.ask: l₁: 3y − 2x = 30; l₂ through A(24, 0) perpendicular to l₁; find, using algebra with working, their intersection P
parts.final_form: coordinates of P with algebraic working
parts.ms: B1 gradient of l₁ = 2/3; M1 l₂ through (24, 0) with the negative reciprocal (y = mx + c must reach c); A1ft y = −(3/2)(x − 24) or 2y + 3x = 72; M1 full method for one coordinate of P (calculator solution of the pair allowed); A1 P(12, 18) (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: l₁ meets the x-axis at B: find the area of triangle BPA
parts.ms: M1 (B1 on ePEN) y = 0 in l₁ for B (x = −15); dM1 correct area method with their −15 and 18, e.g. ½ × 39 × 18 (shoelace or other valid methods fine; B must lie on the x-axis); A1 351 cso (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: sketch y = 2(x + 1)(x − 3)², showing where C cuts or meets the axes
parts.final_form: labelled sketch: positive cubic touching the x-axis at the repeated root
parts.ms: M1 positive cubic shape with one maximum and one minimum; A1 reaches the x-axis at −1 and has its minimum touching at x = 3 (must not stop or cross there); B1 y-intercept 18 consistent with the sketch (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Write f(x) in the form ax³ + bx² + cx + d
parts.final_form: expanded cubic with a, b, c, d found
parts.ms: M1 multiply out (square (x − 3) then multiply by (2x + 2), or equivalent); A1 two terms of 2x³ − 10x² + 6x + 18; A1 all correct; 'simplifying' by dividing by 2 loses the last A1 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Hence find the equation of the tangent to C at x = 1/3
parts.ms: B1ft f′(x) = 6x² − 20x + 6 (ft only from a four-term cubic; product rule fine); M1 attempt f′(1/3); A1 f′(1/3) = 0 from a correct derivative; A1 tangent y = 512/27 (exact), all previous marks in (c) needed (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Sign = kite OABC (OA = OC = 0.6 m, AB = CB = 1.4 m, angles OAB = OCB = 2 rad) joined to sector OCXA; making the method clear, show angle AOC = θ = 1.64 rad to 3 s.f.
parts.final_form: given value to 3 s.f.; method must be made clear (stated in the question)
parts.ms: M1 cosine rule for OB (or OB²); A1 OB = awrt 1.74; dM1 sine rule (or cosine rule) with sides and angles placed correctly and inverse sine to find AOB (or ABO then angle sum); A1* θ = 2 × 0.822 = 1.64 with no rounding slips (doubling 0.827 to state 1.64 loses it); working backwards from 1.64 to recover BC = 1.4 or OC = 0.6 also accepted (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: Find the perimeter of the sign
parts.ms: M1 0.6 × an allowable angle (2π − 1.64 or π − 1.64) or circumference minus minor arc (major arc ≈ 2.79); A1 total 0.6(2π − 1.64) + 2.8 = awrt 5.6 m (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: Find the area of the sign (kite plus major sector)
parts.ms: M1 major sector ½ × 0.6² × (2π − 1.64) (≈ 0.835) or circle minus minor sector; M1 kite area 0.6 × 1.4 sin 2 (or half of it, or OCA + ABC); ddM1 complete correct total; A1 awrt 1.6 m² (degrees route equally creditable) (MS pp.16–19)

parts.ask: y = 4 + 12x − 3x²: (i) write in the form a + b(x + c)²; (ii) hence state the maximum point M
parts.final_form: completed-square form with a, b, c; coordinates of M
parts.ms: (i) M1 complete the square (b = ±3 or c = ±2), or compare coefficients; A1 two of a = 16, b = −3, c = −2; A1 16 − 3(x − 2)² (16 − 3(2 − x)² scores M1A1A0). (ii) B1ft x = 2 or y = 16, B1ft M(2, 16); reversed coordinates SC B1B0 (MS p.20)

parts.ask: l₁ passes through O and M; l₂ is parallel to l₁ and touches C: find an equation of l₂
parts.ms: M1 l₂: y = 8x + k (gradient of OM, ft); dM1 set 4 + 12x − 3x² = 8x + k and reach a 3TQ; A1 3x² − 4x + k − 4 = 0; ddM1 b² − 4ac = 0 to find k; A1 y = 8x + 16/3. Alt: dy/dx = 8 gives contact point (2/3, 32/3), then find k (MS pp.20–21)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: f(x) = √x with P(9, 3); sketch and label y = f(2x) and y = f(x) + 3 on the given diagram
parts.final_form: two labelled curves, each with the image of P stated
parts.ms: M1 one correct labelled curve (f(2x) from O staying above f(x); f(x) + 3 from the positive y-axis, same shape); A1 that curve with its image point, (4.5, 3) or (9, 6); A1 both curves and both points correct; best single diagram is marked (MS pp.22–24)

parts.ask: The graphs meet at Q: show the x-coordinate of Q satisfies √x = 3(√2 + 1)
parts.final_form: given equation reached with surd manipulation shown
parts.ms: B1 √x + 3 = √(2x); M1 write √(2x) as √2√x and collect terms in √x ((√2 − 1)√x = 3); A1* rationalise to √x = 3(√2 + 1) with the multiplying-by-conjugate step shown. Alt: square to a 3TQ in √x and solve (giving both roots scores A0) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: Hence find the coordinates of Q in simplest form
parts.ms: M1 square the given expression to α + β√2; A1 x = 9(3 + 2√2) = 27 + 18√2; B1 y = 3√2 + 6 (√(18√2 + 27) + 3 unsimplified scores B0); working must appear in (c) (MS pp.22–23)

parts.ask: x > 0, f′(x) = ax − 12x^(1/3), f″(x) = 0 when x = 27: find a
parts.ms: B1 f″(x) = a − 4x^(−2/3); M1 set f″(27) = 0 and solve for a; A1 a = 4/9 (common slip a = −4/9 leads to c = 11/9) (MS pp.25–26)

parts.ask: The curve passes through (1, −8): hence find f(x)
parts.ms: M1 integrate with one term correct and indices processed, e.g. (a/2)x² or −9x^(4/3); A1ft (a/2)x² − 9x^(4/3) + c (must include + c); dM1 use (1, −8) with numerical a to find c; A1 f(x) = (2/9)x² − 9x^(4/3) + 7/9 (MS pp.25–26)

parts.ask: Integrate 8x³/5 − 2/(3x⁴) − 1 with respect to x
parts.final_form: each term in simplest form, plus constant of integration
parts.ms: M1 raise one power (x³ → x⁴, x⁻⁴ → x⁻³ or 1 → x); A1 two correct terms, unsimplified fine (+c not counted); A1 two of (2/5)x⁴, (2/9)x⁻³, −x simplified; A1 (2/5)x⁴ + (2/9)x⁻³ − x + c all on one line (2/(9x³) fine); spurious ∫ or '= 0' with no clean expression loses the final mark (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Express f(x) = 11 − 4x − 2x² in the form a + b(x + c)²
parts.final_form: a + b(x + c)² with integers a, b, c
parts.ms: B1 b = −2 (taking out −2); M1 complete the square, (x ± 1)² ± …, or compare coefficients for c; A1 13 − 2(x + 1)² (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Sketch y = f(x), showing the y-intercept
parts.final_form: sketch of the (negative) quadratic with the y-axis crossing labelled
parts.ms: M1 ∩-shaped parabola on axes; A1 cuts the x-axis once either side of O, maximum in quadrant 2, y-intercept (0, 11) marked; graphs symmetric about the y-axis not accepted (MS pp.8–9)

parts.ask: Write down the equation of the line of symmetry of C
parts.ms: B1ft x = −1 (ft x = −c) (MS pp.8–9)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: expand f(x) = (x + √2)² + (3x − 5√8)²
parts.final_form: ax² + bx√2 + c with integers a, b, c
parts.ms: B1 √8 = 2√2 seen or implied; M1 expand both brackets to x² + a√2x + 2 + bx² − c√8x + d form; A1 10x² − 58√2x + 202 (−60√2x signals the B1 was missed) (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Solve √3(4y − 3√3) = 5y + √3 (no calculator)
parts.final_form: p + q√3 with p, q simplified fractions (denominator rationalised)
parts.ms: No calculator. M1 expand and collect the y terms on one side; dM1 make y (or ky) the subject, e.g. y = (9 + √3)/(4√3 − 5); ddM1 rationalise the denominator, multiplication shown; A1 y = 57/23 + (41/23)√3 with all stages seen ((57 + 41√3)/23 not accepted). Alts: substitute y = p + q√3 and compare parts, or square to 23y² − 82√3y + 78 = 0 (MS pp.10–12)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: find, using algebra, the intersections P and Q of x + y = 6 and y = 6x − 2x² + 1
parts.final_form: coordinates of P and Q, found algebraically
parts.ms: No calculator, answers only 0/4. M1 combine to a 3TQ (2x² − 7x + 5 = 0); M1 solve with a correct intermediate line (factorised form, formula with values, or completed square); dM1 find y for one x; A1 (1, 5) and (2.5, 3.5) correctly paired (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Use inequalities to define the region R bounded by C, l and the x-axis
parts.final_form: set of inequalities in x and y
parts.ms: M1 any two, A1 any three, A1 all four of y ≥ 6x − 2x² + 1, x + y ≤ 6, x ≥ a (1 ≤ a ≤ 2.5), y ≥ 0 (strict or non-strict, need not be consistent); using R in place of x or y scores 0; 'or' or ∪ between them loses the last mark (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Semicircular garden radius 3 m, chord BD parallel to diameter AE, angle BOA = 0.7 rad: show angle BOD = 1.742 rad to 4 s.f.
parts.final_form: given value to 4 s.f.; working must lead to it (show-that)
parts.ms: B1* angle BOD = π − 2 × 0.7 = 1.742 (or show the angles sum to π) with a minimal conclusion; degrees route via 99.8° fine (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the area of the flowerbed (segment bounded by chord BD and arc BCD)
parts.ms: M1 triangle BOD = ½ × 3² × sin 1.742 (awrt 4.43); dM1 segment = ½ × 3² × 1.742 − triangle (or semicircle minus triangle minus two small sectors); A1 awrt 3.4 m², no isw if other areas added (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find the perimeter of the flowerbed
parts.ms: M1 a correct method for BD (cosine rule, 2 × 3 cos 0.7, etc., awrt 4.59) or for arc BCD = 3 × 1.742 (5.226); dM1 perimeter = arc + BD, both by correct methods; A1 awrt 9.8 m, no isw (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: x > 0, f′(x) = (x + 3)²/(x√x), P(4, 20) on C: (i) find the gradient at P; (ii) hence find the tangent at P
parts.final_form: (ii) ax + by + c = 0 with integers a, b, c
parts.ms: (i) B1 f′(4) = 49/8; (ii) M1 line through (4, 20) with their gradient (perpendicular gradient M0; y = mx + c must reach c); A1ft correct equation in any form; A1 49x − 8y − 36 = 0 or integer multiple (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Find f(x) (expand, write as powers of x, integrate, use P to find c)
parts.ms: M1 square the numerator and split into powers, one correct index; A1 x^(1/2) + 6x^(−1/2) + 9x^(−3/2); dM1 raise a power by 1; A1 two of (2/3)x^(3/2), 12x^(1/2), −18x^(−1/2); A1 all three (+c condoned); M1 use (4, 20) in the integrated function for c; A1 f(x) = (2/3)x^(3/2) + 12x^(1/2) − 18x^(−1/2) − 1/3, exact coefficients, isw unless multiplied through (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: f(x) = (x + 4)(x − 2)(2x − 9); y = f(x) − p passes through (0, 50): find p
parts.ms: M1 f(0) = 4 × −2 × −9 = 72 and subtract 50 (50 − 72 is M0); A1 p = 22 cao (MS p.19)

parts.ask: y = f(x + q) passes through the origin: write down the possible values of q
parts.ms: B1 one of −4, 2, 4.5; B1 all three and only these (sign-changed values withhold it) (MS p.19)

parts.ask: Find f′(x) (expand the cubic then differentiate)
parts.ms: M1 expand to ax³ + bx² + cx (+d); A1 2x³ − 5x² − 34x (+72); M1 reduce a power by 1; A1 f′(x) = 6x² − 10x − 34 from a correct expansion (wrong, not just missing, constant gives A0) (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Hence find the range of x for which the gradient of y = f(x) is less than −18
parts.final_form: a quadratic-inequality solution set in x
parts.ms: M1 set their f′(x) = −18 and solve 6x² − 10x − 16 = 0 (stated critical values allowed); dM1 choose the inside region; A1 −1 < x < 8/3 with some working ('or' or ∪ not accepted) (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Find the gradient of l₁: 2x − 5y + 7 = 0
parts.ms: B1 gradient 2/5 (or 0.4), identified in (a), not just read off a rearranged equation (MS p.21)

parts.ask: l₂ passes through A(6, −2) perpendicular to l₁: find l₂
parts.ms: M1 perpendicular gradient −5/2; M1 line through (6, −2) with the changed gradient (y = mx + c must reach c); A1 y = −(5/2)x + 13 oe (MS p.21)

parts.ask: Using algebra (no calculator solutions), find the intersection M of l₁ and l₂
parts.final_form: coordinates of M with working shown
parts.ms: Coordinates with no algebra score 0. M1 solve l₁ and l₂ simultaneously for x or y; dM1 find the other coordinate; A1 M(4, 3) (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Diagonals of square ABCD meet at M: find the coordinates of C
parts.ms: B1 x = 2 or y = 8; B1 C(2, 8) (reversed (8, 2) scores B1B0) (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Sketch y = 1/x² − 9
parts.final_form: sketch showing axis intersections and stating equations of asymptotes
parts.ms: B1 1/x²-type shape anywhere on axes (two branches rising steeply near the y-axis and levelling off, no turning points); B1 x-intercepts (±1/3, 0) with a corresponding sketch; B1 one asymptote stated, x = 0 or y = −9; B1 both; the sketch takes precedence over contradictory text (MS pp.24–25)

parts.ask: D: y = kx² meets C at 4 distinct points: find the range of k
parts.ms: B1 k < 0; M1 set 1/x² − 9 = kx² and multiply by x² to a quartic; M1 discriminant of the 3TQ in x², 81 + 4k; A1 critical value −81/4 from correct working (sign slip in rearranging gives A0A0); A1 cso −81/4 < k < 0 in terms of k ('or', comma or ∪ not accepted) (MS pp.24–25)

parts.final_form: simplified terms plus constant of integration
parts.ms: M1 raise any power by 1 (x⁵ → x⁶, x³ → x⁴, x⁻² → x⁻¹; unprocessed x⁵⁺¹ accepted); A1 two terms correctly integrated, unsimplified fine but indices processed; A1 two correct simplified terms on one line; A1 (5/3)x⁶ + (3/2)x⁴ + 3/x + c all simplified on one line (no 1.67x⁶; spurious ∫/dx or multiplying through to clear fractions loses it) (MS p.7)

parts.ms: M1 sine rule sin x/21 = sin 25/13 with sides and angles placed correctly; A1 sin x = awrt 0.6827, isw (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Given AB is the longest side, find x (ambiguous case: the angle opposite the longest side is the largest)

parts.ms: M1 inverse sine of their value (awrt 43°); M1 obtuse angle 180 − arcsin 0.6827, no reason needed (AB longest so the angle opposite it is largest); A1 x = awrt 136.95, A0 if two angles given; cosine-rule route (AC = 9.533) also credited (MS p.8)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: show that (√180 − √80)/√5 is an integer and find its value
parts.final_form: integer value with surd simplification shown
parts.ms: No calculator, all stages shown. M1 √180 = 6√5 or √80 = 4√5 (or √(180/5) = √36, or multiply by √5 to √900, √400); A1 (6√5 − 4√5)/√5 = 2√5/√5 = 2; big jumps without these steps score M0A0 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Rationalise and simplify (4√5 − 5)/(7 − 3√5)
parts.final_form: a + b√5 with a, b rational; working shown (no calculator)
parts.ms: M1 multiply numerator and denominator by 7 + 3√5; dM1 denominator 49 − 45 = 4 and numerator expanded with four terms seen; A1 25/4 + (13/4)√5 (6.25 + 3.25√5 fine; (25 + 13√5)/4 alone not accepted unless a and b then stated). Alt: (4√5 − 5) = (a + b√5)(7 − 3√5), solve 7a − 15b = −5, 7b − 3a = 4 (MS pp.9–10)

parts.final_form: sketch stating coordinates of the maximum and minimum and the equation of the asymptote
parts.ms: B1 same shape translated down (minimum left of the y-axis, maximum right of it); B1 asymptote labelled y = −1, below the x-axis, both ends level; B1 maximum (3/2, 0) on the positive x-axis and minimum (−1, −2) in quadrant 3, marked on the graph; marks independent, no misread credit for y = f(x − 2) (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: On a separate diagram sketch y = f(−x)
parts.final_form: sketch stating coordinates of the maximum and minimum and the equation of the asymptote
parts.ms: B1 reflection in the y-axis (maximum in quadrant 2, minimum on the positive x-axis); B1 asymptote labelled y = 1; B1 maximum (−3/2, 2) and minimum (1, 0) in the right places; no misread credit for y = −f(x) (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Quadratic f(x) has maximum turning point (−2, 12) and crosses the negative x-axis at −5: find f(x)
parts.ms: M1 quadratic form using two facts, e.g. 12 − a(x + 2)², a(x − 1)(x + 5), or ax² + bx + c with two points (a = ±1 condoned for M1 only); A1 correct form with only a (or one equation) left to find; dM1 full method for f(x) using the remaining fact; A1 f(x) = 12 − (4/3)(x + 2)² or −(4/3)(x − 1)(x + 5) or −(4/3)x² − (16/3)x + 20/3 (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: l₁: y = (4/5)x; l₂ is perpendicular to l₁ through (−5, 0): find an equation of l₂
parts.final_form: y = mx + c with m and c stated
parts.ms: M1 perpendicular gradient −5/4; M1 line through (−5, 0) with the changed gradient (y = mx + c must reach c); A1 y = −(5/4)x − 25/4, in the form y = mx + c (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Define the shaded region R (bounded by C, l₁ and l₂ in Figure 2) using inequalities
parts.final_form: set of inequalities in x and y
parts.ms: M1 two of y ≥ −(5/4)x − 25/4, y ≥ (4/5)x, y ≤ −(4/3)x² − (16/3)x + 20/3 (ft their (a) and (b); strict also fine; R in place of y scores M0); A1ft all three, strictness consistent; harmless extra restrictions ignored, restricting ones (e.g. y ≥ 0) penalised; final answer marked, no isw (MS pp.12–14)

parts.ask: All stages of working, no calculator: from 2xy − 3x² = 50 and y − x³ + 6x = 0, show that 2x⁴ − 15x² − 50 = 0
parts.final_form: given equation reached by substitution, with working shown
parts.ms: M1 substitute y = x³ − 6x into the first equation (or an equivalent elimination); A1* 2x⁴ − 12x² − 3x² − 50 = 0 → 2x⁴ − 15x² − 50 = 0 cso, with the two x² terms first shown uncollected (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Hence solve the simultaneous equations (quadratic in x²)
parts.final_form: all valid (x, y) pairs in fully simplified surd form; reject impossible x² values
parts.ms: No calculator. M1 solve the quadratic in x² by factorising (2x² + 5)(x² − 10), formula or completing the square; A1 x² = 10 (or x = ±√10); M1 y = (√10)³ − 6√10 by a non-calculator method; A1 one pair, e.g. (√10, 4√10); A1 cso both pairs (√10, 4√10) and (−√10, −4√10), clearly paired, no extras (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: x > 0, f′(x) = 2/√x + A/x² + 3 and f″(x) = 0 when x = 4: find A
parts.ms: M1 differentiate f′(x), one power reduced by 1; A1 f″(x) = −x^(−3/2) − 2Ax⁻³; dM1 set f″(4) = 0 and solve for A; A1 A = −4 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Given f(x) = 8√3 when x = 12, find f(x) with each term in simplest form
parts.final_form: f(x) with the constant evaluated exactly; each term simplified (the √3 terms cancel, so the constant is rational)
parts.ms: M1 integrate f′(x), one power raised by 1; A1ft 4x^(1/2) − Ax⁻¹ + 3x (+c); dM1 use f(12) = 8√3 to find c with their A; A1ft c = −109/3 (ft A/12 − 36, since f(12) = 8√3 − A/12 + 36 + c; awrt 1 d.p.); A1 f(x) = 4√x + 4/x + 3x − 109/3, not ft; multiplying through by 3 afterwards gives A0 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Ceiling-fan section: sector OAB radius 9 cm with arc AB = 15 cm, sector OBCD radius 84 cm, angle AOD = 2π/3: show arc CD = 35.9 cm to 1 d.p.
parts.final_form: given value; show enough working to justify 35.9 to 1 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 arc AB: 15 = 9θ, θ = 5/3; dM1 angle for arc CD = 2π/3 − 5/3 (≈ 0.4277); A1* cso arc CD = 84(2π/3 − 5/3) = 35.929… shown to at least 2 d.p. before giving 35.9 cm (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Find the perimeter of the whole fan face (three congruent sections)
parts.ms: M1 perimeter = 3 × 15 + 3 × 35.9 + 6 × (84 − 9), all six arcs and radial edges (implied by awrt 603); A1 awrt 603 cm (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Find the surface area of the fan face according to the flat-surface model
parts.final_form: 3 significant figures with units made clear (cm²)
parts.ms: M1 one relevant area (e.g. blade sector ½ × 84² × (2π/3 − 5/3) ≈ 1510); dM1 a second area that combines with it (inner sector ½ × 9² × 5/3 = 67.5); A1 both correct (angles to 3 s.f.); ddM1 correct combination, ×3; A1 awrt 4730 cm² or 0.473 m², units required, isw (MS pp.17–19)

parts.ask: Given sin α = p (0 < α < 90°), state in terms of p: 2 sin(180° − α), sin(α − 180°), 3 + sin(180° + α)
parts.ms: B1 2p; B1 −p; B1 3 − p (each accepted as the y-coordinate of a stated point) (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: On the copy of the graph of y = sin x, sketch y = sin 2x
parts.ms: M1 sine-shaped curve from O with the same amplitude (scaling may be off; one full cycle on one side enough); A1 correct, crossing at (180, 0) and (360, 0), two cycles each side of the y-axis (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Hence find, in terms of α, the x-coordinates in 0 < x < 180° where sin 2x = p
parts.final_form: all solutions in the interval, in terms of α
parts.ms: B1 x = α/2; M1 a second solution by symmetry (e.g. (180 − α)/2, 90 + α/2, 180 + α/2), range not yet checked; A1 x = 90 − α/2 as the second solution with no extra solutions in range (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Find dy/dx for y = (2/7)x³ + (1/7)x² − (5/2)x + k
parts.ms: M1 at least two terms correct; A1 dy/dx = (6/7)x² + (2/7)x − 5/2, isw (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: The normal l to C at A (x = −7/2) is also a tangent to C at B: show the x-coordinate of B satisfies 12x² + 4x − 33 = 0
parts.final_form: given equation reached with working shown
parts.ms: M1 substitute x = −7/2 into dy/dx (gradient 7); M1 perpendicular gradient −1/7 for the tangent at B; dM1 set dy/dx = −1/7; A1* 12x² + 4x − 35 = −2 → 12x² + 4x − 33 = 0 with an intermediate line; no credit carried back from (d) (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Hence find the x-coordinate of B, justifying the choice of root
parts.final_form: one exact value with a reason for rejecting the other root (e.g. from the figure)
parts.ms: M1 solve the quadratic, e.g. (2x − 3)(6x + 11) = 0 (calculator allowed); A1 x = 3/2 with a reason from the sketch, e.g. B has positive x so not −11/6 (MS pp.21–22)

parts.ask: Given the y-intercept of l is −1, find k
parts.ms: M1 l: y = −(1/7)x − 1 from their changed gradient; dM1 coordinates of A (−7/2, −1/2) or B (3/2, −17/14) from l; ddM1 substitute into the equation of C and solve for k; A1 cso k = 5/4. Alts: y-coordinate in terms of k then intercept of l = −1, or equate l with C and use the known root (MS pp.21–23)

parts.ask: Differentiate y = x³/4 − x² + 17/x (x > 0), giving dy/dx in simplest form
parts.final_form: simplified dy/dx on one line; no +c; do not multiply through by 4
parts.ms: M1 power reduced by 1 on any term; A1 two of (3/4)x², −2x, −17x⁻² (indices processed); A1 all three on one line, simplified; final A1 withheld if terms multiplied by 4 or +c appears (MS p.7)
parts.er: Integrating instead of differentiating scored 0; usual slips were one wrong term, e.g. 17/x becoming −17x or a wrong coefficient on the x³/4 term (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the equation of the tangent to C at R(2, 13/2) in the form ax + by + c = 0 with integer a, b, c
parts.final_form: ax + by + c = 0 with integer coefficients, all terms on one side; an equation, not an expression
parts.ms: M1 substitute x = 2 into a changed dy/dx (gradient −21/4); dM1 line through (2, 13/2) with that gradient (not the normal gradient; if y = mx + c used, must reach c = …); A1 21x + 4y − 68 = 0 or any integer multiple (MS p.7)
parts.er: One mark commonly lost for wrong form, a sign slip or writing an expression not an equation; more lost by using y instead of dy/dx for the gradient or finding the normal (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Expand (x − 5)(2x + 1)(x + 3) ≡ ax³ + bx² − 32x − 15 to find a and b
parts.ms: B1 a = 2; B1 b = −3; values embedded in a correct cubic accepted and take precedence over contradictory stated values (MS p.8)
parts.er: Expansion mostly correct; miscopying the coefficients when stating a and b was condoned (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Integrate (x − 5)(2x + 1)(x + 3)/(5√x) with respect to x, writing each term in simplest form
parts.final_form: four simplified terms in fractional powers plus +c; exact fractions (4/35 must be a fraction, not a rounded decimal); no integral sign or dx left in the answer
parts.ms: M1 split into a sum of powers of x (one correct index); A1 two terms of (2/5)x^(5/2) − (3/5)x^(3/2) − (32/5)x^(1/2) − 3x^(−1/2); M1 raise a non-integer power by 1; A1 two integrated terms correct; A1 (4/35)x^(7/2) − (6/25)x^(5/2) − (64/15)x^(3/2) − 6x^(1/2) + c all simplified on one line (MS p.8)
parts.er: Errors: multiplying coefficients instead of dividing by 5, adding on the denominator term, trying to simplify using the factorised form, mishandling fractional powers, sign slips, omitting +c (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Linear model V = pt + q for a share price (£1.05 at t = 3, £1.65 at t = 5): find p and q
parts.ms: M1 form two simultaneous equations and solve for p or q (or gradient (1.65 − 1.05)/(5 − 3)); A1 p = 0.3 or q = 0.15; A1 both (MS p.9)
parts.er: Most successful question; calculator solution of the simultaneous equations was acceptable on this occasion; errors were slips or p and q swapped (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Use the model to find T when the price is £2.50, to one decimal place
parts.ms: M1 use their p, q with V = 2.5 and rearrange T = (2.5 − q)/p; A1 7.8 cao, isw (MS p.9)
parts.er: Most common error was not giving the answer to 1 d.p. (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Detailed reasoning required, no calculator solutions: solve f(x) = x²(2x + 1) − 15x = 0
parts.final_form: all three roots, with the factorised (or formula/completed-square) working shown; roots must match the factorisation
parts.ms: M1 expand and take out x to reach a quadratic factor (2x² + x − 15); dM1 solve the quadratic by factorising, formula or completing the square (stated roots must match the factorisation); B1 two of x = 0, 5/2, −3; A1 all three; correct answers alone do not earn full marks (MS p.10)
parts.er: Disappointing: too many did not show detailed reasoning, worked backwards from a calculator so the factorised form did not match the quadratic, or left solutions incomplete (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Hence solve y^(4/3)(2y^(2/3) + 1) − 15y^(2/3) = 0 for y > 0 (substitution x = y^(2/3))
parts.final_form: single positive solution in simplified surd form; reject y = 0 and the negative value
parts.ms: M1 set y^(2/3) = 5/2 (a positive root from (a)) and show how the fractional power is handled, e.g. y² = 125/8 or y = (5/2)^(3/2); decimals or a bare answer score M0; A1 cso (5/4)√10 only (MS p.11)
parts.er: Many jumped straight to the answer without the fractional-power step; others kept y = 0 and/or y = −(5/4)√10 despite y > 0 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: All stages of working required: given f′(x) = 12/√x + x/3 − 4 and P(9, 8) on C, find f(x) in simplest form
parts.final_form: simplified exact coefficients with the constant evaluated; no rounded decimals, no integral sign or "= 0"
parts.ms: M1 raise one power by 1; A1 two of 24x^(1/2), x²/6, −4x; A1 all three (+c condoned); dM1 substitute (9, 8) to find c (impossible without +c); A1 f(x) = 24x^(1/2) + x²/6 − 4x − 83/2, not made into integer coefficients (MS p.12)
parts.er: Main error was dividing by 1/2 when finding the coefficient of the root term; omitting +c capped the question at three marks (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the coordinates of the point where the normal to C at P crosses the y-axis
parts.final_form: coordinates (0, y), not just a value of c
parts.ms: M1 evaluate f′(9) (= 3); dM1 negative reciprocal −1/3; M1 normal through (9, 8) with x = 0 (changed gradient); A1 (0, 11) (MS pp.12–13)
parts.er: Some substituted y = 0 or used the tangent; stating only c = 11 did not fully answer (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Given 0 < k < 4, sketch y = (2x − k)(x + 4)², showing axis intercepts in terms of k
parts.final_form: labelled sketch: positive cubic touching the x-axis at (−4, 0), crossing at (k/2, 0), y-intercept (0, −16k)
parts.ms: B1 positive cubic with a maximum and a minimum; B1 crosses at x = k/2 right of the y-axis and has a turning point at x = −4; B1 y-intercept −16k below the x-axis; graph labels take precedence over separate statements (MS p.14)
parts.er: Errors: negative cubic, curve through the origin, crossing instead of touching at (−4, 0), several curves for chosen k values, missing axis labels (ER p.5)

parts.ask: On separate axes sketch y = k/x²
parts.final_form: two branches in quadrants 1 and 2 approaching the coordinate axes
parts.ms: B1 correct shape in quadrant 1 or 2 not crossing the axes; B1 both branches, nothing in quadrants 3–4; withheld if asymptotes other than the axes are drawn (MS p.15)
parts.er: Errors: horizontal asymptote at y = k, only one branch, branches in quadrants 1 and 3, curves in all four quadrants (ER p.5)

parts.ask: State, with a reason, the number of roots of (2x − k)(x + 4)² = k/x²
parts.final_form: number of roots with a reason referring to intersections of the two curves (not axis crossings)
parts.ms: B1 one root because the two graphs intersect once; needs both sketches of correct shape and position in (a) (MS p.15)
parts.er: Some answered two roots from the cubic's x-intercepts; algebraic attempts failed; must make clear it is the curves' intersection (ER p.5)

parts.ask: From a graph of y = f(x) through P(−4, 6), Q(−1, 6), R(2, 6), S(3, 6), find the values of x for which f(x) < 6
parts.final_form: strict inequalities in x; the inside interval written as one combined inequality
parts.ms: M1 one end of the inside region; A1 −1 < x < 2 (two separate inequalities without "and" not enough); B1 x < −4, x > 3 (MS p.16)
parts.er: Critical values usually found but inequality signs wrong; some could not find the inside region (ER p.5)

parts.ask: State the largest solution of f(2x) = 6
parts.er: Some listed several solutions without identifying the largest (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Sketch y = f(−x) and state the images of P, Q, R and S
parts.final_form: reflection in the y-axis with the four image coordinates stated
parts.ms: B1 reflection in the y-axis with the higher maximum in quadrant 1; B1 two correct points (or all x or all y coordinates); B1 all four correct (MS pp.16–17)
parts.er: Most reflected correctly; some lost the higher turning point in quadrant 1; some reflected in the x-axis (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find the set of x for which f(−x) ≥ 6 and x < 0
parts.final_form: one closed interval (non-strict inequalities) and nothing else
parts.ms: B1 −3 ≤ x ≤ −2 only; open interval or OR/union notation not accepted (MS p.17)
parts.er: Extra inequalities alongside the correct one lost the mark (ER pp.5–6)

parts.ask: Pond plan: major sector AOBX (radius 3 m, angle AOB = 2π/3) — find the exact area of the sector
parts.ms: B1 reflex angle 4π/3; M1 ½r²θ with r = 3; A1 6π exact (MS p.18)
parts.er: Too many gave a decimal rather than the exact value (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the exact perimeter of sector AOBX
parts.final_form: exact; arc length plus two radii
parts.ms: M1 rθ with r = 3 and the sector angle; A1 4π + 6 exact (MS p.18)
parts.er: Many forgot to add the two radii; rounded decimals lost the A1 (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the exact area of triangle AOB
parts.ms: M1 ½ab sin C with 3, 3, 2π/3 (or two right triangles); A1 9√3/4 (MS p.18)
parts.er: Mostly correct; decimal-only answers lost the A1 (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Show that AB = 3√3 m
parts.final_form: given answer: show a simplified intermediate result such as AB² = 27
parts.ms: M1 cosine rule (or sine rule or two right triangles); A1* 3√3 with no errors and a simplified step such as AB² = 27 seen (MS pp.18–19)
parts.er: Most scored only 1/2: insufficient steps for a show-that, especially via the cosine rule (ER p.6)

parts.ask: With BC = 8 m and angle BCA = π/6, find the total area of the pond to 2 significant figures
parts.ms: M1 sine rule for sin BAC or angle BAC (or cosine-rule quadratic for AC); A1 sin BAC = 4√3/9 or BAC ≈ 0.88; M1 area ABC = ½(3√3)(8)sin(π − π/6 − BAC); dM1 add sector + AOB + ABC; A1 awrt 43 (exact 6π + 2√11 + 41√3/4 accepted) (MS pp.18–19)
parts.er: Many got the sine-rule step; errors came from the wrong angle for ABC (using the sin BAC value, or subtracting from 2π) (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Write ½x² − 10x + 22 in the form a(x + b)² + c
parts.final_form: completed-square form with a, b, c found; do not multiply through by 2
parts.er: Errors mostly in b (e.g. 20) and the constant (c = 22 or −78); show working even without the emboldened instruction (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Deduce the coordinates of the minimum point M
parts.ms: B1ft one coordinate; B1ft (10, −28), following (−b, c) from (a) (MS pp.20–21)
parts.er: Best done from (a); many restarted with dy/dx = 0, also successful (ER p.7)

parts.ask: The normal l to C at P has equation y = k − x/8: find the coordinates of P
parts.ms: B1 tangent gradient 8; M1 dy/dx = x − 10 set equal to 8 and solved (alt: tangent-line discriminant); A1 x = 18; A1 y = 4 (MS pp.20–21)
parts.er: Usually all or nothing; many treated l's gradient as the tangent gradient and set the discriminant of l with C to zero, scoring 0 (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Find the value of k
parts.ms: dM1 substitute (18, 4) into y = k − x/8; A1 k = 25/4 (MS pp.20–21)
parts.er: Those correct in (c)(i) almost always scored both marks (ER p.7)

parts.ask: Give the inequalities defining region R bounded by l, C and the vertical line through M
parts.final_form: three inequalities in x and y, strict or non-strict used consistently
parts.ms: B1ft one, B1ft two, B1 all three of x ≥ 10, y ≤ 25/4 − x/8, y ≥ ½x² − 10x + 22; strictness consistent for the last mark (MS pp.20–21)
parts.er: Lost for inequality signs reversed (esp. for y), inequalities in terms of k or R, or a wrong k (ER p.7)
